history.text: Sixteen-twenty. The sun's gone behind Pabbay and taken the colour with it.
Dark as a press up here. The cells are flat again. The engineer's been saying since Easter they're tired.
Sunday the fourteenth of November. I wrote the date at the top of the page this morning and sat looking at it.
Twenty-one winters on the lights, and the wind still sounds like someone trying the door.
The phone's been dead since the September gale. The radio's all the company there is till Thursday.
The torch first, top shelf by the door. Then the engine, and the lights. Then lighting-up time, and the long quiet.
She catches on the second turn and settles into that low knock you feel through your boots.
The lamps come up. That's better.
Fourteen amps and climbing. She'll come up.
Mind the temperature. That engine was old when Father was keeper.
Now, lighting-up time. The console, under the east window.
[A carrier on Channel 16. Two clicks. No voice.]
Somebody keyed a set on sixteen. Twice. Nobody spoke.
Some boy with his father's handset. On the Sabbath. His mother'll skelp him.
The motor takes up the optic overhead. Twelve turns a minute, same as the day they fitted it.
Normal power. Forty miles on a clear night. Tonight won't be clear.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, North Point, this is Stornoway Coastguard, Stornoway Coastguard. Evening radio check, over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Stornoway, North Point. Reading you loud and clear, over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Loud and clear also. Anything to report? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Light exhibited at sixteen-forty. Engine running, batteries on charge. Nothing on the radar. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Roger. Gale warning for Hebrides and Minches. South-westerly seven, rising severe gale nine before dawn. Visibility poor in rain. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Received. Gale nine before dawn. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: And Callum. It's the fourteenth.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I know what night it is, Morag.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Aye. I thought you might. I'll be on till six. Shout if you want company on the set. Stornoway out.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: North Point Light, North Point Light, this is the Kittiwake, Kittiwake, eh, Sierra Yankee three-seven. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Kittiwake, North Point. Go ahead, over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: Callum, is that you? Thank God. Sorry, eh, North Point. I'm coming in from the Flannans, and the rain's that thick I can't see my own bow. I was meant to pick up the Sound an hour ago. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: And, eh. Don't be telling my mother I was out on the Sabbath. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: I've stopped her. I'm just sitting here like a gull on a fence post. Can you put me in? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Stay where you are, Rory. I'll find you. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: Holding. Holding. Right. I'm holding. Over.
First I need to know where he is. The radio at the desk. Ask him to confirm his position.
Bearing and range from the light. On the radar he's that echo north of the reef, a little east of the dashed line.
The North Sound runs straight in on oh-oh-oh. Bring his head round thirty degrees at a time until he's pointing down the line.
Once he can see the light and he's on the line, he'll find the channel buoys himself.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: North Point, Kittiwake! I've got the green on the Sound. I've got it! Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Keep it fine on your starboard bow and come in slow. North Point. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: Aye. Aye, I see it. Here, Callum, you'll laugh, but my grandfather used to say there's a boat out in the East Gut on nights like this. No lights. Just waiting. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Your grandfather said a lot of things, Rory.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: He did. He did. Half of them were true, mind. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: I'm in the Sound now. Thanks, North Point. I'll stand you a dram at Christmas. Kittiwake out.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Are you awake over there? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Stornoway, North Point. Wide awake. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Good. The set's quiet and the kettle's broken. Talk to me. Off the log, Callum.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: What's on your mind, Morag?

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Donald's birthday would have been Thursday. Nine years. You'd think it would get easier, wouldn't you.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: It doesn't get easier. You just get stronger arms.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Aye. That's about it. Your father used to say that. About the lamp-room weights.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Is it true what they say in Tarbert? Twenty-one years and you've never once missed lighting-up?

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Never once.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Like father, like son. He kept that station like a kirk, so they say.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Stornoway listening on sixteen. Out.
Eighteen-thirty, radio check, gale warning. Ten to seven, Kittiwake in by the North Sound. Twenty-three-twenty-five, Stornoway on sixteen. All well.
The same small square letters I learned at the school in Tarbert. Father always said I wrote like a clerk.

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...North Point... North Point... this is... Mary Ellen... Mary Ellen...

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...we cannot see your light... repeat... we cannot see your light...

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Vessel calling North Point, say again your name. Over.

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...Mary... Ellen...
Static. Then nothing. Not even the carrier.
The light is burning. I can hear the motor through the ceiling.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Callum. Did you hear that? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I heard it.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Mary Ellen. Somebody's idea of a joke. On this night. I'll find out who. Stornoway out.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Go ahead, Morag.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: I've rung round. Nobody's reporting a Mary Ellen. The register's had nothing by that name since nineteen fifty-three. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Lost with seven of the eight aboard, the skipper among them. Presumed. You know all this.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I know it.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Aye. You would.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Callum. You were on the light that night. With your father.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I was there. I was twenty-three.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: I know. I took the call. I was twenty-six and it was my first winter on the set.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Watch your radar. If somebody's out there playing silly beggars, they're close. That signal was strong. Stornoway out.
There. An echo. Bearing oh-four-six, a hundred yards off the East Gut rocks.
Not moving. Not fading with the sweep the way sea clutter does.
...And now it's gone. Sea clutter. It has to be sea clutter.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: North Point, this is the schooner Gannet. Hector Macleod. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Gannet, North Point. Go ahead, Hector.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: I've two passengers sick as dogs and no stars to steer by. I'm somewhere west of you, I think. I'd take a bearing kindly. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Confirm your position and I'll talk you through the West Gut. Over.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: Right you are. I'm in your hands, North Point. Over.
West Gut, three-one-four. Line her up on the dashed line and she'll do the rest.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: Gannet's in the Gut and the passengers have stopped praying. Grand job, North Point. Over.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: Here. Tell your father I was asking for him. Oh. Och, I'm sorry, Callum. Thirteen years and I still forget. Gannet out.
